matched_rules.because: The datacenter control system was in the process of failing away from one of its control hosts, which is the exact 'when' condition for R-003.
The control system is unavailable (minimum visibility) and cooling did not transition to maximum cooling or purge mode in part of the datacenter, matching R-004's 'when' conditions.
Mechanical cooling is down (cooling system shut down) and servers have begun shutting down due to overheating, indicating the thermal buffer is depleting and automated shutdowns have started.

next_actions.action: Manually investigate the affected cooling equipment, check the PLCs controlling the air handling units, reset affected equipment and PLCs into maximum cooling configuration, and confirm cooling is restored and temperatures are falling before standing down.

Treat the failover as a period of elevated risk to cooling availability, watch the cooling plant directly, expect that a fault in control system logic can make the control system unresponsive, and verify that cooling systems have actually entered their designed maximum-cooling fallback.

Treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted; expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin, and recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down.

escalate.reason: Thermal buffer depletion is imminent or automated shutdowns have started (EC2 servers shutting down due to overheating), and the control system failover is in progress with cooling not transitioning to maximum cooling or purge in part of the datacenter.

per_finding.note: R-003 warns that a fault in control system logic can make the control system unresponsive, but does not name the excessive interactions or third-party bug mechanism.
R-004's condition and action directly address cooling not transitioning to maximum cooling in part of the datacenter.
R-004 directs checking and resetting PLCs, pointing at the right component, but does not identify PLC failure as the cause of purge mode not working.
R-004's condition explicitly notes the control system is unavailable, matching the minimum visibility finding.
R-004's next action is exactly to manually investigate, reset affected equipment, and put it into maximum cooling configuration.
The triage does not mention disabling failover mode or any interim remediation to prevent recurrence.
The triage does not mention training local operations teams or building confidence to reset before customer impact.
The triage does not mention modifying air handling units so purge mode bypasses PLC controllers.
R-002 warns that hardware can be damaged before shutdown, pointing at hardware failure, but does not mention longer recovery or instance retirement.
